newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Monetary Exchange plans 5-yr bond futures.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Monetary Exchange plans 5-yr bond futures.

text.p: The Malaysia Monetary Exchange (MME) will launch a five-year bond futures contract, Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar said on Wednesday.
"The Malaysia Monetary Exchange has formed a bond committee to introduce a five-year bond futures contract," he said at the opening of a seminar on interest rate futures organised by MME.

He said this would speed the growth of a debt market in Malaysia, which expects to mobilise nearly 385 billion ringgit in private investment during the Seventh Plan period to the year 2000 against 207.4 billion raised in the previous five-year period.
He said a large part of these funds would come from the capital markets.
However, the minister said no date had been set to launch the contract as the committee was still finalising details.
MME started in May with a futures contract based on the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR). The contract goes up to three years forward.
